title: Minimum Number of Visited Cells in a Grid
summary: Given an m x n grid starting at (0, 0), you can move rightward to (i, k) where j < k ≤ grid[i][j] + j or downward to (k, j) where i < k ≤ grid[i][j] + i.
statement: Given an m x n grid starting at (0, 0), you can move rightward to (i, k) where j < k ≤ grid[i][j] + j or downward to (k, j) where i < k ≤ grid[i][j] + i. Find the minimum number of cells to visit to reach (m - 1, n - 1), or return -1 if no path exists.
constraints: Start at the top-left cell and count it as visited.
From (r,c), move right or down by between one and grid[r][c] cells.
Return the minimum cells visited to reach bottom-right, or -1 if unreachable.
hints: Process cells in row-major order; every legal predecessor is above or left and is already processed.
Maintain a min-heap per row and column keyed by predecessor distance, with its farthest reachable coordinate.
Discard expired heap entries, take the smaller live predecessor distance, then add one and publish this cell to both heaps.
Heaps expose the best still-reaching predecessor; row-major direction makes the dynamic program acyclic and each heap entry is inserted and removed once.
editorial: Heaps expose the best still-reaching predecessor; row-major direction makes the dynamic program acyclic and each heap entry is inserted and removed once.

tests.explanation: A shortest valid route reaches the destination after visiting four cells.
The destination cannot be reached because all routes stop before it.
